panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). Disease attribution is direct from the SMARD1 case-report title and caption. [raw subtype: SMARD1] B: Panel B shows slow myosin heavy chain immunostaining of the same SMARD1 muscle biopsy: hypertrophic fibers with predominant slow (type I) expression (compensatory type I fiber hypertrophy) alongside atrophic fibers also expressing slow HC, confirming ongoing neurogenic atrophy in this patient. [raw subtype: SMARD1] C: Panel C shows fast myosin heavy chain immunostaining highlighting atrophic fibers in the SMARD1 muscle biopsy, consistent with...

in_text_mentions: Electrophysiological examinations at 11 months of age demonstrated complete denervation in the most distal muscles (tibialis anterior, gastrocnemius, and foot muscles) and severely reduced interference pattern in the most proximal ones (vastus lateralis, deltoid, and facial muscles) (Table 1). At that age, marked atrophy of both type I and type II fibers was found in muscle biopsy (Figure 1C) with fibers showing prominent nuclei and increased oxidative activity, clearly demonstrative of a neurogenic process (Figure 1D) showing features of immature fetal phenotype (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E muscle biopsy from a patient ultimately diagnosed with SMA type 3; caption specifically notes central nuclei and splitting fibers, but large group atrophy was not observed, making the appearance atypical for SMA. [raw subtype: type_3] B: NADH-TR stain from a genetically confirmed SMA type 3 patient; caption says neurogenic change was not observed except for a few small angular fibers, which is a nonspecific/atypical histological finding for SMA. [raw subtype: type_3] C: ATPase pH 4.5 histochemistry from the same SMA type 3 patient; shows type 1 fiber predominance, which can be seen in chronic SMA but is not by itself diagnostic. [raw subtype: type_3] D: ATPase pH 10.6 histochemistry from the same SMA type 3 patient; shows type 1 fiber predominance with rare type 2B fibers, consistent with a chronic neurogenic/myopathic pattern in SMA but not definitive alone. [raw subtype: type_3]

panels.figure_caption: Muscle biopsy from left brachioradialis at the age of 46 years (A) Hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining. The central nuclei (arrowhead) and splitting fibers (arrow) were observed. Connective tissue was slightly increased. Large group atrophy fibers were not observed. (B) Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide dehydrogenase‐tetrazolium reductase (NADH-TR) staining. The neurogenic change was not observed except for a few small angular fibers (arrow). (C, D) Adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase) staining (pH 4.5 and 10.6). Type 1 fiber predominance was observed and type 2B fiber was rarely observed. Type 2C fiber was not seen.
in_text_mentions: Her symptoms gradually increased in severity, and she required a cane to walk at the age of 39 years. At the age of 46 years, she was hospitalized for the second time. Because the creatinine kinase (CK) level was at the upper limit of the normal range or slightly elevated and muscle specimens from the left brachioradialis muscle showed a predominance of type 1 fiber (Figures 1A-1D), she was tentatively diagnosed with myopathy of an unknown etiology. She had not been prescribed any medication such as glucocorticoids but had been followed up in the outpatient clinic.
